question: I really love the choice of words in the summaries of the original novels. Who usually writes those summaries? Is it you personally?
answer:
There are summaries on the back of the books, and despite the strict character-count limitations, Nagasaki, the author of the original work, writes them himself with great effort.

I like fluffy, vague-feeling summaries, so I write summaries with that kind of fluffy feeling to them. For the final line, I created a template along the lines of, “The hugely popular web novel, the ___ and ___, Act ,” but after doing this for 45 volumes, there aren't really any four-character compounds left that I can use in the “ and ___” part anymore!

I thought I was doing my best to avoid repeating them, but when I made a list of them the other day, there were a ton of repeats (laughs). I put a lot of effort into that part too, so I'd be happy if you paid attention to it. If you get the chance, please take a look at the summaries as well.
